strengths.I007: Learns from real blinded verdicts, with nuisance covariates (length, hedges, family match) zeroed at selection, and falls back to the current ranking when labels are scarce. It is cheap and testable offline with leave-one-brief-out AUC.
strengths.I005: Replaces persuasive critique prose with executable checks and library lookups, so survival in critique and selection depends on falsified claims rather than eloquence. This is an external signal a lone agent lacks, and it is measurable as falsified-claim rate on an on/off switch.

verdicts.reason: I005 changes what survives critique using tool-grounded evidence a single agent cannot supply, while I007 only re-ranks finalists and needs 15+ labelled briefs and non-panel labels that may not exist.

strengths.I003: Cheap scoring-only change (about 60 lines) that optimises expected best-of-3 under correlated same-lever ideas, and can be tested by replaying saved records.
strengths.I001: Puts extra critique and mutation effort on the ideas near the top-3 cutoff, so it improves the ideas themselves at the development stage rather than only which ones are picked. It has an on/off comparison at equal tokens, same-length edits, a length cap and a different-family judge as safeguards against gaming.

verdicts.reason: I001 can raise the quality of the delivered ideas through an independent-signal refinement loop, while I003 only re-selects among existing finalists and risks a null result or a loss on mean rating.

strengths.I008: Explicitly models judge discrimination, position bias and self-preference, fitted against external verdicts, at zero extra tokens. Its effect is testable offline against external strengths.
strengths.I003: Selects the 3 to maximise the expected best idea, using mechanism clusters to avoid delivering three variants of one lever. It gives the user real choice and fits how users use a shortlist.

verdicts.reason: I003 needs no hundreds of past external-labelled votes or stable judge reliability, and it improves what users get on any brief by delivering a portfolio, whereas I008's gain depends on untested judge stability and can reduce to uniform weighting.

strengths.I002: Adds cross-run learning of which edit types work, with a measurable child-beats-parent outcome and negligible token cost. It is a mechanism unique to a multi-run system with an idea library.
strengths.I008: Corrects position and self-preference bias in the finals judges using parameters fitted to external raters, and can be validated offline on existing runs at equal vote count.

verdicts.reason: I008 is built to remove known judge biases and calibrate to external raters, whereas I002 depends on an unbuilt contest loop, needs a warm-up of 20 briefs, and risks learning in-loop judge quirks with effects too small to detect.
